NN/g, “Neobrutalism: Definition and Best Practices”

A usability firm’s definition of the style, with accessibility guidance.

Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Definition: “Neobrutalism (or neubrutalism), an evolution of traditional brutalism, is a visual-design trend defined by high contrast, blocky layouts, bold colors, thick borders, and ‘unpolished’ elements.”

It separates the two: brutalist sites “might use plain HTML elements and limited color palettes” (example: Drudge Report), while neobrutalist designs “are likely to be more colorful and orderly”.

On shadows: “solid, single-color shadows (e.g., a black drop shadow offset by 4px)”. Examples include Gumroad, Figma, 99percentoffsale.com, byooooob.com, cyanbanister.com, dodonut.com, and bieffeforniture.it.

Best practices: meet contrast ratios, limit the palette to 2 or 3 bold colors, pair chunky headings with neutral body fonts, and pad dense shapes with 24 to 32 px.

Why it belongs

Useful for attestation of the name and for the brutalism versus neobrutalism distinction. Some of its examples lean retro or brutalist rather than outline-and-shadow, so each needs a capture.
